synopsis: The booklet requires the operating design domain to be written first, in October 2026, before scenarios, sites or sample sizes are planned, and recommends coverage through domain attributes, equivalence classes and interactions rather than repeated site names [f13253, f13251]. The proposed combinations exceed 7,000 cells, making 59–299 physical trials in every cell impractical; the indicative physical anchor matrix instead comprises roughly 60–100 instrumented runs per machine family [f5206, f5469, f6177]. Coverage must distinguish forward, reverse, start-from-rest, turning and swing, include degraded and recovery cases, and report safety-critical detection performance per cell rather than as one aggregate [f2996, f10778, f5454]. Correlated models should support large-matrix virtual regression, but simulation is not sole evidence; Euro NCAP's on-road precedent verifies randomly selected prediction-grid cells physically [f881, f1607, f1755]. No universal off-road coverage prescription or standardised national matrix in the reviewed India DGMS guidance was found, and neither scenario counts nor perfect sensor models establish adequate coverage [f5475, f2453, f10506, f5108]. Plans should leave uncovered cells visibly blank and predeclare primary statistical claims because checking hundreds of cells at 95% confidence produces chance passes or failures [f9479, f12172].
